description: Packages checked by the compatibility table. See docs/guide/packages.md.

packages.name: bcrypt
packages.notes: Native addon; bcryptjs is the pure-JS alternative.

packages.name: jsdom
packages.notes: jsdom runs scripts with node:vm and starts workers with node:worker_threads, which workerd does not implement; use cheerio or linkedom on Workers.

packages.name: got
packages.notes: With the http2 option, got calls node:tls.connect with options that Workers reject, and the default options work.

packages.name: undici
packages.notes: undici fails on workerd because node:tls.connect rejects its ALPNProtocols option; use the global fetch on Workers.

packages.name: firebase
packages.notes: The SDK is for clients: the ai audio and messaging/sw subpaths need browser APIs, and server code uses firebase-admin.

packages.name: @sentry/node
packages.notes: The Node SDK needs node:child_process, node:worker_threads and node:perf_hooks, which workerd does not implement, and its ./import hook calls node:module.register, which Bun mocks; use @sentry/cloudflare or @sentry/bun.

packages.name: better-sqlite3
packages.notes: Native addon. On workerd, process.report.getReport() returns an empty object with no header. The package reads header.glibcVersionRuntime, so the run throws a TypeError before it reaches the native addon.

packages.name: @noble/hashes
packages.notes: The root entry throws on purpose and asks for an import of a submodule, so the row checks sha2, the most used one.

packages.name: @noble/curves
packages.notes: The root entry throws on purpose and asks for an import of a submodule, so the row checks secp256k1, the most used one.

packages.name: firebase-admin
packages.notes: On Workers the default credentials of google-auth-library start the gcloud command with child_process.

packages.name: @google-cloud/storage
packages.notes: The default credentials of google-auth-library start the gcloud command with child_process, which a Worker cannot run.

packages.name: mssql
packages.notes: The tedious driver uses UDP for a named instance, and @azure/identity starts a browser with child_process, and a Worker cannot do either. Tedious calls an @azure/identity credential only after a SQL Server accepts the login, so a run without one cannot reach the child_process calls. The UDP lookup for a named instance does not throw on workerd, and the connection times out.

packages.name: argon2
packages.notes: argon2 is a native addon, so use bcryptjs or a WebAssembly hash on Workers.

packages.name: @electric-sql/pglite
packages.notes: PGlite calls WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming only in its browser branch. With nodejs_compat at the date of the table, PGlite takes its Node branch on workerd, so this call does not run. The Node branch reads its files from disk, and the Worker bundle has none, so PGlite.create() fails before it uses WebAssembly or reaches node:process.binding. The multi-tab worker of PGlite uses navigator.locks, which Bun and workerd do not have.

packages.name: socket.io
packages.notes: On Workers the browser build of engine.io-parser reads a Blob with FileReader, which Workers do not have.
